title: A BioBrick-Compatible Vector for Allelic Replacement Using the XylE Gene as Selection Marker
author: Casanova, Pasotti, et al.
materials: Details about pBBknock thermosensitive sequence design). The vector also carries a chloramphenicol resistance cassette (BBa_P

TOP10 (Invitrogen) were used for cloning according to manufacturer's instructions. For gene knockout experiments, the W strain (ATCC 9637) was transformed by a standard heat shock protocol [32]. Strains were routinely grown in LB medium; chloramphenicol (12.5 mg/l) or ampicillin (100 mg/l) were added as required. Catechol (C9510, Sigma Aldrich) was dissolved in deionized water to obtain a 10 mM stock that was prepared fresh every day. Primers used in this work are listed in Additional file 1: Table S1.

The pBBknock vector was specialized to delete the ldhA gene of E. coli W by assembling the ldhA flanking DNA fragments (A and B, both 0.9 kbp-long, see Fig. 1b) in the cloning site. A and B regions were separately amplified from the genome of E. coli W with primer pairs PAtail_F/PAtail_R and PBtail_F/PBtail_R, respectively, with Phusion Hot Start Flex polymerase (New England Biolabs). Each PCR product was purified (NucleoSpin Extract II, Macherey-Nagel), digested with EcoRI and PstI (Roche), purified again, and finally individually ligated (T4 ligase, Roche) into the EcoRI-PstI-digested pSB1A2 vector [19]. Each construct was sequence-verified with standard BioBrick™ primers VF2 and VR. The A and B fragments in pSB1A2 were then digested with SpeI-PstI and XbaI-PstI, respectively, and ligated according to the BioBrick™ Standard Assembly to yield the AB construct (in pSB1A2), which was sequence-verified and, upon EcoRI-PstI digestion, finally ligated into pBBknock.

The assay was performed as described by Massaiu et al. [23]. Cultures grown to saturation at 37 °C at 220 rpm in 2 ml of LB with 100 mM phosphate buffer and 40 g/l glucose, were 100-fold diluted in 9 ml of the same medium and grown for 4 h. One ml of culture was centrifuged (13,000 rpm, 1 min), washed with 1 ml of 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.3 and the pellet was resuspended with 0.4 ml of CelLytic B (Sigma Aldrich), supplemented with a protease inhibitor cocktail, to lyse the cells. After 10 min at room temperature, cell debris were removed by centrifugation (13,000 rpm, 5 min) and the supernatant was assayed. Reaction mix (180 μl), containing 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.3, 0.4 mM NADH and 10 mM sodium pyruvate, was mixed with 20 μl of lysate and absorbance at 340 nm (OD340) was monitored at 25 °C every 5 min in an Infinite F200 (Tecan) microplate reader. The slope of the absorbance time series, proportional to enzymatic activity of the sample, was computed via linear regression. Protein quantification in the lysate was obtained via Micro BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Scientific). Specific enzymatic activity was calculated by dividing the total enzymatic activity by protein level and expressed as 104*OD340/min/μg of cell protein.

The copy number of pBBknock was estimated by comparing it to the one of pSB4C5 [19], which carries a non-ts pSC101 origin. To this aim, the BBa_J107029 part containing a constitutive promoter driving the Red Fluorescent Protein (RFP) expression, was assembled in both vectors upon EcoRI-PstI digestion. Transformed TOP10 cells were assayed both in selective LB and M9 supplemented medium (11.28 g/l M9 salts - M6030, Sigma Aldrich, 2 mM MgSO4, 0.1 mM CaCl2, 2 g/l casamino acids, 1 mM thiamine hydrochloride and 4 ml/l glycerol) as previously reported [20], except that cultures were always incubated at 30 °C. RFP synthesis rate per cell (Scell), expressed in arbitrary units (AU), was computed and assumed to be proportional to the plasmid copy number. Scell and cell growth rate were computed as previously described [20]. Results were expressed as average Scell values of at least three biological replicates and the confidence intervals of Scell mean were reported.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and media
steps.instruction: Prepare LB broth and add chloramphenicol to 12.5 mg L⁻¹ or ampicillin to 100 mg L⁻¹ as required; dissolve catechol (C9510, Sigma‑Aldrich) in deionized water to make a 10 mM stock fresh each day.

steps.title: Heat‑shock transform strain W
steps.instruction: Transform E. coli W (ATCC 9637) by a standard heat‑shock protocol (Invitrogen), recover, and plate on LB agar containing chloramphenicol (12.5 mg L⁻¹) at 30 °C.

steps.title: PCR amplify flanking regions
steps.instruction: Amplify the 0.9 kbp left (A) and right (B) homology arms from E. coli W genomic DNA using primer pairs PAtail_F/PAtail_R and PBtail_F/PBtail_R with Phusion Hot‑Start Flex polymerase (NEB).

steps.title: Purify and digest PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify each PCR product with NucleoSpin Extract II (Macherey‑Nagel), digest with EcoRI and PstI (Roche), and purify the digested DNA again.

steps.title: Ligate fragments into pSB1A2
steps.instruction: Ligate each EcoRI‑PstI‑digested fragment into EcoRI‑PstI‑digested pSB1A2 vector using T4 DNA ligase (Roche), transform TOP10 cells, and verify each construct by sequencing with standard BioBrick primers VF2 and VR.

steps.title: Assemble AB construct in pSB1A2
steps.instruction: Digest the A‑containing pSB1A2 with SpeI‑PstI and the B‑containing pSB1A2 with XbaI‑PstI, ligate the two fragments together according to the BioBrick Standard Assembly to generate the AB construct in pSB1A2, sequence‑verify, then excise the AB fragment with EcoRI‑PstI.

steps.title: Insert AB into pBBknock
steps.instruction: Ligate the EcoRI‑PstI‑released AB fragment into EcoRI‑PstI‑digested pBBknock vector using T4 DNA ligase (Roche) and transform TOP10 cells for propagation.

steps.title: Transform knockout construct into W
steps.instruction: Transform the pBBknock‑AB plasmid into E. coli W by heat‑shock, recover, and plate on LB + chloramphenicol (12.5 mg L⁻¹) at the permissive temperature (30 °C) to select for integration of the first recombination event.

steps.title: Screen for vector excision
steps.instruction: Incubate colonies at 42 °C to cure the temperature‑sensitive pBBknock; screen for white colonies on catechol plates (colorimetric xylE assay) and confirm gene deletion by colony PCR.

steps.title: Measure LDH activity
steps.instruction: Grow cultures in 2 mL LB containing 100 mM phosphate buffer and 40 g L⁻¹ glucose at 37 °C, 220 rpm to saturation; dilute 100‑fold into 9 mL of the same medium and grow 4 h. Centrifuge 1 mL at 13 000 rpm for 1 min, wash with 1 mL 100 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.3, resuspend pellet in 0.4 mL CelLytic B (Sigma‑Aldrich) plus protease inhibitor cocktail, incubate 10 min at room temperature, centrifuge 13 000 rpm for 5 min and collect supernatant. Prepare a 180 µL reaction mix containing 100 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.3, 0.4 mM NADH and 10 mM sodium pyruvate, add 20 µL lysate, and monitor absorbance at 340 nm (OD₃₄₀) every 5 min at 25 °C in a Tecan Infinite F200. Determine the slope (activity) by linear regression. Quantify protein in the lysate with the Micro BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Scientific) and calculate specific activity as 10⁴ × OD₃₄₀ min⁻¹ µg⁻¹ protein.

steps.title: Estimate plasmid copy number
steps.instruction: Assemble the BBa_J107029 part (constitutive promoter driving RFP) into both pBBknock and pSB4C5 via EcoRI‑PstI cloning, transform TOP10 cells, and grow cultures in selective LB and in M9‑supplemented medium (11.28 g L⁻¹ M9 salts, 2 mM MgSO₄, 0.1 mM CaCl₂, 2 g L⁻¹ casamino acids, 1 mM thiamine HCl, 4 mL L⁻¹ glycerol) at 30 °C. Measure RFP synthesis rate per cell (Scell) in arbitrary units using the method of [20]; assume Scell is proportional to plasmid copy number. Compute Scell and growth rate as described in [20] for at least three biological replicates and report the mean Scell with confidence intervals.
